Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Arkansas. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Arkansas:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Arkansas Federal Bankruptcy Data

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 90 days (60(b))/ reasonable time window in Arkansas.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Arkansas because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Arkansas, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

## California Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/california.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

California Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for California residents.

California Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

California gives debtors roughly 6 months to vacate a default judgment on enumerated grounds (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 473(b), 473(d)). This is tighter than the federal 1-year standard in many jurisdictions. Voidable-judgment relief is still available afterward for jurisdictional defects or improper service.

RuleCalifornia Standard

Primary rule citationCal. Code Civ. Proc. 473(b), 473(d)

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)6 months (473(b))

Window for void judgment2 years (473(d) void)

473(b) is California's primary tool: mandatory relief for attorney-fault default if affidavit filed within 6 months; 473(d) sets aside void judgments up to 2 years.

How California Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Attorney's sworn affidavit of fault is a game-changer; the relief is mandatory, not discretionary.

The universal thread across most California cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. California courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in California, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most California courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in California. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in California:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Window to vacate (ordinary)4 months

Delaware distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 6 months (60(b)(1-3)) window in Delaware.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Delaware because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Delaware, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Delaware means test to see if you qualify.

## District of Columbia Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/district-of-columbia.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

District of Columbia Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for District of Columbia residents.

District of Columbia Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

District of Columbia generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under D.C. Super. Ct. R. 55(c), 60(b). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleDistrict of Columbia Standard

Primary rule citationD.C. Super. Ct. R. 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

DC courts apply Johnson v. Lustine Realty Co. factors; fast cure if moved quickly.

How District of Columbia Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Meritorious defense + actual notice timing + prejudice balance.

The universal thread across most District of Columbia cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. District of Columbia courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - District of Columbia Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in District of Columbia, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most District of Columbia courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in District of Columbia - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in District of Columbia. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in District of Columbia:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in District of Columbia

District of Columbia distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) window in District of Columbia.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in District of Columbia because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in District of Columbia, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the District of Columbia means test to see if you qualify.

## Florida Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/florida.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Florida Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Florida residents.

Florida Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Florida generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.540(b). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleFlorida Standard

Primary rule citationFla. R. Civ. P. 1.540(b)

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (1.540(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Florida courts apply the Winter Park Publishing three-prong excusable-neglect + due-diligence + meritorious-defense test.

How Florida Courts Evaluate Your Motion

File within 1 year; sworn affidavit detailing excusable neglect is standard.

The universal thread across most Florida cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Florida courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Florida Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Florida, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Florida courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Florida - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Florida. When you were never served at all, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable) and can be challenged at any time under Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.540(b)(4). Be careful, though: if service was attempted with defects but you actually learned of the lawsuit, Florida courts treat the judgment as merely voidable, and the one-year deadline generally applies (Kozinski v. Phillips, 126 So. 3d 1264 (Fla. 4th DCA 2013)).

Common service defects in Florida:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Florida Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Florida debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 46,008 consumer bankruptcy cases from Florida's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 724,38994.2%5.1%

Chapter 1321,61951.3%48.6%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Florida

Florida distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (1.540(b)(1-3)) window in Florida.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Florida because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Florida, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Florida means test to see if you qualify.

## Georgia Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/georgia.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Georgia Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Georgia residents.

Georgia Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Georgia has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (O.C.G.A. Section 9-11-55, 9-11-60) imposes a 15 days auto-open / reasonable time deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleGeorgia Standard

Primary rule citationO.C.G.A. Section 9-11-55, 9-11-60

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)15 days auto-open / reasonable time

Window for void judgment3 years (void)

Georgia's 15-day 'open default as a matter of right' window is unique; miss it and discretionary relief still available within a reasonable time.

How Georgia Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Pay accrued costs; file sworn answer within 15 days to open default automatically.

The universal thread across most Georgia cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Georgia courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Georgia. Chapter 796998.6%0.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

## Idaho Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/idaho.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Idaho Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Idaho residents.

Idaho Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Idaho gives debtors roughly 6 months to vacate a default judgment on enumerated grounds (Idaho R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)). This is tighter than the federal 1-year standard in many jurisdictions. Voidable-judgment relief is still available afterward for jurisdictional defects or improper service.

RuleIdaho Standard

Primary rule citationIdaho R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)6 months (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Idaho's 6-month window is among the tightest in the Northwest.

How Idaho Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Good-cause standard; Wolford v. Wolford excusable-neglect analysis.

The universal thread across most Idaho cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Idaho courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

Idaho enforces a reasonable-time limit measured from when you learned of the judgment, so act promptly once you find out it exists.

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Illinois Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Illinois residents.

Illinois Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Illinois has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (735 ILCS 5/2-1301, 5/2-1401) imposes a 30 days (Section 2-1301) / 2 years (2-1401) deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleIllinois Standard

Primary rule citation735 ILCS 5/2-1301, 5/2-1401

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)30 days (Section 2-1301) / 2 years (2-1401)

Window for void judgment30 years (void)

Illinois has two distinct windows: 30-day motion to vacate under 2-1301 with near-automatic relief; 2-1401 petition up to 2 years requires due diligence + meritorious defense.

How Illinois Courts Evaluate Your Motion

The 30-day 2-1301 window is near-automatic; miss it and 2-1401 standard is much harder.

The universal thread across most Illinois cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Illinois courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Illinois, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Illinois courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Illinois. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. "Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Illinois Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Illinois debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 9,898 consumer bankruptcy cases from Illinois's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 76,72999.5%0.4%

Chapter 133,16945.9%53.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Illinois

Illinois distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 30 days (Section 2-1301) / 2 years (2-1401) window in Illinois.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Illinois because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Illinois, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Illinois means test to see if you qualify.

## Indiana Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/indiana.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Indiana Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Indiana residents.

Indiana Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Indiana generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under Ind. T.R. 60(B). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleIndiana Standard

Primary rule citationInd. T.R. 60(B)

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year ((1),(2),(3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time ((4-8))

Indiana T.R. 60(B) closely tracks federal rule; local practice allows expanded grounds.

How Indiana Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show meritorious defense + one enumerated ground within 1 year.

The universal thread across most Indiana cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Indiana courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Indiana Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Indiana, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Indiana courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Indiana - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Indiana. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Indiana:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Indiana Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Indiana debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 3,325 consumer bankruptcy cases from Indiana's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 779297.5%2.0%

Chapter 132,53369.8%29.5%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Indiana

Indiana distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year ((1),(2),(3)) window in Indiana.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Indiana because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Indiana, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Indiana means test to see if you qualify.

## Iowa Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/iowa.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Iowa Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Iowa residents.

Iowa Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Iowa has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Iowa R. Civ. P. 1.977) imposes a 60 days deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleIowa Standard

Primary rule citationIowa R. Civ. P. 1.977

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)60 days

Window for void judgment1 year (void)

Iowa's 60-day window is among the shortest; post-60-day relief requires extraordinary circumstances.

How Iowa Courts Evaluate Your Motion

File within 60 days or lose ordinary relief; Iowa follows strict-compliance model.

The universal thread across most Iowa cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Iowa courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 60 days window in Iowa.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Iowa because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

RuleKansas Standard

Primary rule citationK.S.A. 60-260(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60-260(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

## Maine Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/maine.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Maine Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Maine residents.

Maine Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Maine generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under M.R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleMaine Standard

Primary rule citationM.R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Maine follows federal-rule framework; liberal relief on pre-judgment defaults.

How Maine Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show mistake, inadvertence, or excusable neglect + meritorious defense.

The universal thread across most Maine cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Maine courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Maine Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Maine, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Maine courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Maine - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Maine. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Maine:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Maine

Maine distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) window in Maine.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Maine because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Maine, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Maine means test to see if you qualify.

Maryland Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

Maryland Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Maryland has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Md. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleMaryland Standard

Primary rule citationMd. Rule 2-535

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)30 days (ordinary) / reasonable time

Window for void judgmentany time (jurisdiction)

Maryland's 30-day revisory-power window is tight; miss it and only 'fraud, mistake, or irregularity' standard applies.

Strict 30-day window for ordinary relief; extraordinary relief for void or fraud judgments.

RuleMassachusetts Standard

Primary rule citationMass. R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Minnesota Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Minnesota residents.

Minnesota Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Minnesota generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under Minn. R. Civ. P. 60.02. After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleMinnesota Standard

Primary rule citationMinn. R. Civ. P. 60.02

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60.02(a)-(c))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (d-f)

Minnesota applies Finden v. Klaas four-factor test (excusable neglect + meritorious defense + reasonable excuse + no prejudice).

How Minnesota Courts Evaluate Your Motion

File within 1 year of entry; courts lenient when default due to procedural confusion.

The universal thread across most Minnesota cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Minnesota courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

P. 60.02(d). Minnesota courts usually vacate such judgments whenever they are discovered, but the state supreme court has enforced the rule’s reasonable-time language against void judgments, so file promptly once you learn the judgment exists.

Common service defects in Minnesota:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

← defaultjudgment.org home

Missouri Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Missouri residents.

Missouri Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Missouri generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under Mo. R. Civ. P. 74.05(d), 74.06. After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleMissouri Standard

Primary rule citationMo. R. Civ. P. 74.05(d), 74.06

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)reasonable time (good cause) / 1 year (mistake)

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Missouri Rule 74.05(d) is liberal: good cause + meritorious defense, no firm time limit for pre-execution relief.

How Missouri Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Set-aside motion particularly effective before execution; courts apply liberal good-cause standard.

The universal thread across most Missouri cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Missouri courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Missouri Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Missouri, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Missouri courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Missouri - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Missouri. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Missouri:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Missouri Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Missouri debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 45,771 consumer bankruptcy cases from Missouri's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 722,13299.0%0.8%

Chapter 1323,63955.1%44.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Missouri

Missouri distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the reasonable time (good cause) / 1 year (mistake) window in Missouri.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Missouri because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Missouri, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Missouri means test to see if you qualify.

## Montana Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/montana.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Montana Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Montana residents.

Montana Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Montana has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Mont. R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)) imposes a 60 days (60(b)(1-3)) deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleMontana Standard

Primary rule citationMont. R. Civ. P. 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)60 days (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Montana's 60-day window is one of the shortest in the West; post-60-day relief requires void judgment or extraordinary circumstances.

How Montana Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Lussy v. Ocwen three-prong test (no culpable conduct + meritorious defense + no prejudice).

The universal thread across most Montana cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Montana courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Montana Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Montana, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Montana courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Montana - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Montana. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Montana:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Montana

Montana distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 60 days (60(b)(1-3)) window in Montana.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Montana because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Montana, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Montana means test to see if you qualify.

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nebraska residents.

Nebraska Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

RuleNebraska Standard

Primary rule citationNeb. Rev. Stat. 25-2001

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 term of court (statutory)

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Nebraska uses unique 'term of court' framework; relief generally available at same term judgment entered.

How Nebraska Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show mistake, inadvertence, neglect, or fraud within same term of court.

## Nevada Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/nevada.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Nevada Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nevada residents.

Nevada Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Nevada gives debtors roughly 6 months to vacate a default judgment on enumerated grounds (NRCP 55(c), 60(b)). This is tighter than the federal 1-year standard in many jurisdictions. Voidable-judgment relief is still available afterward for jurisdictional defects or improper service.

RuleNevada Standard

Primary rule citationNRCP 55(c), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)6 months (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Nevada Yochum v. Davis four-factor test.

How Nevada Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show prompt action + meritorious defense + no prejudice + good cause.

The universal thread across most Nevada cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Nevada courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

## New Jersey Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/new-jersey.html

New Jersey Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New Jersey residents.

New Jersey Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

New Jersey generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under N.J. Ct. R. 4:50-1. After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleNew Jersey Standard

Primary rule citationN.J. Ct. R. 4:50-1

Answer deadline (from service)35 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (R.4:50-1(a)-(c))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (d-f)

New Jersey's Mancini v. EDS 'exceptional circumstances' analysis; courts liberal when due process concerns present.

How New Jersey Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show excusable neglect + meritorious defense; void-judgment relief not time-limited.

The universal thread across most New Jersey cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. New Jersey courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Court Rule 4:50-1(d). New Jersey still requires the motion within a reasonable time, and its courts have denied relief after long unexplained delays, so file promptly once you learn the judgment exists.

Common service defects in New Jersey:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

## New Mexico Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/new-mexico.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

New Mexico Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New Mexico residents.

New Mexico Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

New Mexico generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under NMRA 1-060(B). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleNew Mexico Standard

Primary rule citationNMRA 1-060(B)

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year ((1),(2),(3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (4-6)

New Mexico tracks federal Rule 60(b); Meiboom v. Watson factors govern.

How New Mexico Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show excusable neglect + meritorious defense; one-year bar on enumerated grounds.

The universal thread across most New Mexico cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. New Mexico courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - New Mexico Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in New Mexico, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most New Mexico courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in New Mexico - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in New Mexico. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in New Mexico:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in New Mexico

New Mexico distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year ((1),(2),(3)) window in New Mexico.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in New Mexico because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in New Mexico, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the New Mexico means test to see if you qualify.

Related New Mexico Resources

Motion to vacate template

Grounds for vacating

How to vacate (step-by-step)

Improper service defense

Meritorious defense

Judgment to garnishment pathway

New Mexico motion-to-vacate rules

New Mexico wage garnishment limits

## New York Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/new-york.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

New York Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

New York Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

New York generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under CPLR 5015(a). After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleNew York Standard

Primary rule citationCPLR 5015(a)

Answer deadline (from service)20-30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (5015(a)(1))

Window for void judgmentno time limit (void)

New York's CPLR 5015(a)(1) provides 1-year window for reasonable excuse + meritorious defense; (a)(4) jurisdiction defects have no time bar.

How New York Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Reasonable excuse + meritorious defense within 1 year of service of notice of entry.

The universal thread across most New York cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. New York courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in New York, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most New York courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in New York. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in New York:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

New York Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how New York debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,231 consumer bankruptcy cases from New York's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 71,14598.7%1.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in New York

New York distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (5015(a)(1)) window in New York.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in New York because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in New York, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

RuleNorth Carolina Standard

Primary rule citationN.C. R. Civ. P. 55(d), 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

North Carolina applies Brown v. Lifford three-factor test.

## Ohio Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

## Oklahoma Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/oklahoma.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Oklahoma Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oklahoma residents.

Oklahoma Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Oklahoma has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (12 O.S. 1031.1) imposes a 30 days (1031.1) / 2 years deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleOklahoma Standard

Primary rule citation12 O.S. 1031.1

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)30 days (1031.1) / 2 years

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Oklahoma's 30-day court-control window followed by 2-year petition period.

How Oklahoma Courts Evaluate Your Motion

File within 30 days for court-control relief; 2-year window for fraud/mistake petition.

The universal thread across most Oklahoma cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Oklahoma courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Oklahoma, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Oklahoma courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Oklahoma. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Oklahoma, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Oklahoma means test to see if you qualify.

## Oregon Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/oregon.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Oregon Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oregon residents.

Oregon Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Oregon generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under ORCP 71. After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleOregon Standard

Primary rule citationORCP 71

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (B(1)-(3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (B(4-5))

Oregon tracks federal Rule 60(b) with minor variations.

How Oregon Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect + meritorious defense.

The universal thread across most Oregon cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Oregon courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Oregon Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Oregon, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Oregon courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Oregon - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Oregon. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Oregon:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Oregon

Oregon distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (B(1)-(3)) window in Oregon.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Oregon because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Oregon, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Oregon means test to see if you qualify.

## Pennsylvania Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/pennsylvania.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Pennsylvania Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Pennsylvania residents.

Pennsylvania Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Pennsylvania has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Pa. R. Civ. P. 237.3, 3051) imposes a 10 days (237.3 auto) deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RulePennsylvania Standard

Primary rule citationPa. R. Civ. P. 237.3, 3051

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)10 days (237.3 auto)

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (fraud/void)

Pennsylvania's 10-day automatic-strike rule (237.3) for defaults entered without 10-day notice is near-automatic.

How Pennsylvania Courts Evaluate Your Motion

File verified answer within 10 days of notice + attached verified answer = mandatory strike.

The universal thread across most Pennsylvania cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Pennsylvania courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Pennsylvania Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Pennsylvania, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Pennsylvania courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Pennsylvania - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Pennsylvania. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Pennsylvania:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Pennsylvania Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Pennsylvania debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,513 consumer bankruptcy cases from Pennsylvania's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7415n/an/a

Chapter 131,098n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Pennsylvania

Pennsylvania distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 10 days (237.3 auto) window in Pennsylvania.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Pennsylvania because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Pennsylvania, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Pennsylvania means test to see if you qualify.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Tennessee because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Tennessee, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Tennessee means test to see if you qualify.
