## Texas Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/texas.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Texas Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Texas residents.

Texas Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Texas has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Tex. R. Civ. P. 320, 329b) imposes a 30 days (plenary) / 2 years (bill of review) deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleTexas Standard

Primary rule citationTex. R. Civ. P. 320, 329b

Answer deadline (from service)20 days (Monday after)

Window to vacate (ordinary)30 days (plenary) / 2 years (bill of review)

Window for void judgmentno time (void)

Texas's 30-day plenary jurisdiction window is firm; post-30-day relief requires bill-of-review showing Craddock factors + prevented presenting defense.

How Texas Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Craddock v. Sunshine Bus Lines test (accident/mistake + meritorious defense + no delay/injury).

The universal thread across most Texas cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Texas courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Texas Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Texas, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Texas courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Texas - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Texas. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable). In Texas the usual vehicle is a bill of review, which must be filed within four years of the judgment; only when the court’s own record shows a complete failure of service can the judgment be collaterally attacked at any time (PNS Stores, Inc. v. Rivera, 379 S.W.3d 267 (Tex. 2012)).

Common service defects in Texas:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Texas Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Texas debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 30,781 consumer bankruptcy cases from Texas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711,84497.8%2.0%

Chapter 1318,93736.8%63.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Texas

Texas distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 30 days (plenary) / 2 years (bill of review) window in Texas.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Texas because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Texas, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Texas means test to see if you qualify.

## Utah Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/utah.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Utah Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Utah residents.

Utah Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Utah has one of the tighter windows in the country to vacate a default judgment. The primary vacatur rule (Utah R. Civ. P. 60(b)) imposes a 90 days ((1),(2),(3)) deadline for most enumerated grounds. After that window closes, only narrow grounds remain (void judgment, jurisdictional defect, or equitable relief).

RuleUtah Standard

Primary rule citationUtah R. Civ. P. 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)21 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)90 days ((1),(2),(3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (4-6)

Utah's 90-day window for enumerated grounds is tight; void-judgment relief not time-limited.

How Utah Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect + meritorious defense within 90 days.

The universal thread across most Utah cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Utah courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Utah Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Utah, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Utah courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Utah - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Utah. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Utah:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Utah

Utah distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 90 days ((1),(2),(3)) window in Utah.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Utah because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Utah, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in West Virginia

West Virginia distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) window in West Virginia.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in West Virginia because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in West Virginia, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the West Virginia means test to see if you qualify.

## Wisconsin Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]
Source: https://defaultjudgment.org/states/wisconsin.html

← defaultjudgment.org home

Wisconsin Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Wisconsin residents.

Wisconsin Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

Wisconsin generally follows the federal 1-year framework for vacating default judgments under Wis. Stat. Section 806.07. After the 1-year window, limited relief remains for void judgments, jurisdictional defects, or fraud.

RuleWisconsin Standard

Primary rule citationWis. Stat. Section 806.07

Answer deadline (from service)20 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year (806.07(1)(a-c))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (void)

Wisconsin applies Baird Contracting v. Mid Wisconsin Bank five-factor test.

How Wisconsin Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show prompt motion + meritorious defense + good cause within 1 year.

The universal thread across most Wisconsin cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Excusable neglect. Genuine accident, illness, or service failure - not mere forgetfulness or choice to ignore.

Meritorious defense. SOL, lack of contract, wrong defendant, paid debt, or FDCPA violation. See the full list.

Prompt motion. Wisconsin courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.

Debt Collector Failure to Appear - Wisconsin Rules

If the collector or plaintiff fails to appear at a required hearing in Wisconsin, you can often move for dismissal with prejudice. The cure rules flip in this scenario:

Status hearing no-show. Most Wisconsin courts enter a dismissal for lack of prosecution after one or two missed appearances.

Garnishment hearing no-show. The writ is quashed and any withheld wages may be ordered returned.

Evidence hearing no-show. If the collector cannot produce a live witness with personal knowledge of the account, the court may sua sponte dismiss.

Many junk-debt buyers lose on failure-to-appear alone because they cannot produce a live witness with knowledge of the original account. Always demand a live witness and attend every hearing.

Improper Service in Wisconsin - The Strongest Ground

Service defects are the most common - and strongest - ground to vacate in Wisconsin. When service was never properly made, the default judgment is void (not merely voidable), which means it can be attacked at any time under most state rules, not just within the ordinary vacatur window. Even so, file promptly once you learn the judgment exists; unexplained delay only invites arguments against you.

Common service defects in Wisconsin:

"Sewer service" - process server lies about delivery and you never receive the summons.

Service on wrong address after you moved.

Substitute service on someone not authorized to accept (e.g., minor child, ex-spouse, neighbor).

Publication service without exhausting personal-service attempts.

Service on a co-defendant rather than you directly.

See improper-service defense deep dive for the affidavit template and evidentiary burden.

Wisconsin Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a default judgment cannot be vacated, bankruptcy's automatic stay freezes collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Wisconsin debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,541 consumer bankruptcy cases from Wisconsin's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 795399.4%0.4%

Chapter 1358848.1%51.9%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Wisconsin

Wisconsin distinguishes extrinsic fraud (cognizable as void-judgment attack, no time limit in most states) from intrinsic fraud (subject to the ordinary vacatur window).

Extrinsic fraud - fraud on the court that prevented you from presenting your defense. Example: the plaintiff lied about your address to prevent service.

Intrinsic fraud - fraud in the evidence or pleadings presented. Example: the plaintiff attached a forged contract. Subject to the 1 year (806.07(1)(a-c)) window in Wisconsin.

Extrinsic fraud is the stronger path in Wisconsin because it is generally not subject to the ordinary time bar.

When Bankruptcy Resolves the Underlying Debt

If you cannot vacate the default judgment in Wisconsin, bankruptcy often remains viable:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt, making the judgment unenforceable as to you personally.

Chapter 13 treats the judgment as a general unsecured claim paid pro rata through the plan.

Judgment lien avoidance under 11 U.S.C. Section 522(f) strips judgment liens that impair your homestead exemption.

Check 1328(f) refiling screener and the Wisconsin means test to see if you qualify.

Wyoming Default Judgment Rules: How to Vacate [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Wyoming residents.

Wyoming Default Judgment Vacatur Rules

RuleWyoming Standard

Primary rule citationWyo. R. Civ. P. 60(b)

Answer deadline (from service)30 days

Window to vacate (ordinary)1 year ((1),(2),(3))

Window for void judgmentreasonable time (4-6)

Wyoming tracks federal Rule 60(b) framework.

How Wyoming Courts Evaluate Your Motion

Show mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect + meritorious defense.

The universal thread across most Wyoming cases: you must show both a procedural excuse (why you did not answer) and a meritorious defense (why you should have won). One without the other rarely succeeds.

Prompt motion. Wyoming courts penalize delay. File immediately after learning of the judgment.

No prejudice to plaintiff. The longer you wait, the more the plaintiff has relied on the judgment.
